scope: Proposition 5.3 (Homogeneous tests imply nefness) of the manuscript “Maximal Seshadri constants on arbitrary polarized surfaces” (preprints/Maximal-Seshadri-Constants-on-Arbitrary-Polarized-Surfaces-September-23-2026/main.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 039 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 85976b9c9ccf5e56), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 16. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: Let S be a smooth integral complex projective surface, let L be ample, and let p1, . . . , pr be distinct points. Put H = L2 and w = p H/r. Suppose that, for all positive integers k, m with m > kw, no nonzero section of L⊗k vanishes to order at least m at every pi. On the blow-up π : Y → S of these points, with exceptional curves Ei, the real divisor class D0 = π∗ L − w r X i=1 Ei is nef.
